articles.title: El Valencia despide a Corberán y al CEO de Fútbol, Ron Gourlay
articles.standfirst: El ejecutivo escocés renovó al técnico en verano hasta 2028 cuando tenía contrato hasta 2027, a pesar del riesgo que suponía la decisión
articles.summary: El ejecutivo escocés renovó al técnico en verano hasta 2028 cuando tenía contrato hasta 2027, a pesar del riesgo que suponía la decisión
articles.body: El Valencia ha despedido al entrenador Carlos Corberán y al CEO de Fútbol, Ron Gourlay, en una decisión que supone un giro radical en la dirección deportiva de la entidad apenas dos meses después de que el club renovara al técnico de Cheste hasta 2028 con el respaldo expreso del propio ejecutivo escocés. De momento, se hará cargo del primer equipo -hay partido el martes en Vitoria ante el Alavés- el técnico del filial Óscar Sánchez. La figura de Corberán estaba cuestionada desde la derrota del equipo en Coruña, calificada por el propio técnico como "vergonzosa" y la nula reacción que hubo en el equipo tanto en los encuentros ante el Barcelona (0-5) y en Sevilla (1-0). Su falta de capacidad para hacer reaccionar al equipo y la escasa empatía de la mayor parte del vestuario -a pesar de algunas manifestaciones públicas de jugadores- el técnico solo ha podido agotar uno de los tres partidos que inicialmente el club se había tomado como margen antes del parón internacional. Tras la derrota en el Sánchez Pizjuán ya quedaba claro que se había quedado al borde del precipicio y que dependía, como el propio Gourlay, de una llamada de Singapur. No hay que olvidar que el presidente Kiat Lim había presenciado el partido del Valencia contra el Barcelona en Mestalla y pudo tener contacto con el vestuario y con otros ejecutivos del club, además del propio Gourlay y del técnico Carlos Corberán. Además, el club comunicó también este domingo la finalización de la relación contractual con Gourlay, así como con los miembros de su equipo de trabajo, Lisandro Isei, Hans Gillhaus, Andrés Zamora y Malek Shafei. Según explicó la entidad, la medida responde a la voluntad de "iniciar una nueva etapa en su estructura deportiva y de gestión del área de fútbol". La salida del ejecutivo británico se produce después de haber liderado algunas de las decisiones deportivas más arriesgadas de los últimos meses, entre ellas la renovación de Corberán hasta junio de 2028. Entonces, el Valencia defendió que el técnico era "la figura idónea para liderar el crecimiento del equipo durante las próximas temporadas" y destacó que la ampliación de contrato contaba con "el total respaldo" de Gourlay. Pero hay más en la decisión tomada con el escocés. El mercado de fichajes del Valencia -en el que también participó el técnico- dejó mucho que desear. El club liberó dos dorsales para traer un delantero y un central, posiciones que finalmente se quedaron sin reforzar. Después, se defendió por los estrechos márgenes del fair play financiero, rechazó la posibilidad de dimitir y recordó que se había marcado un plazo de tres años para culminar su proyecto en el Valencia. En el comunicado oficial emitido a primera hora de la tarde (última hora en Singapur), la entidad recuerda que el entrenador llegó a Mestalla "con el objetivo de liderar el proyecto deportivo en una situación compleja que pudo revertir" y destaca que desempeñó su labor "con profesionalidad, pasión y máximo compromiso" a lo largo de 72 partidos oficiales. El club agradeció tanto al técnico valenciano como a sus colaboradores el trabajo realizado durante su estancia al frente del equipo y evitó avanzar detalles sobre las razones que han motivado la rescisión de sus contratos. Asimismo, el Valencia anunció que dará a conocer "próximamente la nueva estructura del área de fútbol y la configuración del próximo proyecto deportivo", una reorganización que marcará el futuro inmediato de la entidad. Mientras se define ese nuevo organigrama, Óscar Sánchez, entrenador del VCF Mestalla, asumirá de manera provisional las tareas del primer equipo. Esta semana hay partido contra el Alavés, en Vitoria, el martes y el domingo, en Mestalla (21:00 horas), frente a la Real Sociedad. En su mensaje final, el Valencia trasladó un mensaje de tranquilidad al entorno y aseguró que mantiene "estabilidad y confianza en el futuro", al tiempo que reafirmó su compromiso con la construcción de un proyecto deportivo "sólido, competitivo y sostenible".

articles.title: Diogo Jota chants: Cristiano Ronaldo demands lifetime bans for fans
articles.summary: Footage on social media appears to show Al-Hilal's Ruben Neves reacting to Al-Taawoun fans chanting Diogo Jota's name at him during their Saudi Pro League match.
articles.body:
Portugal star Cristiano Ronaldo has called for lifetime bans to be issued to fans who chanted the late Diogo Jota's name towards his international team-mate Ruben Neves.

Liverpool forward Jota died in a car crash at the age of 28 in July last year, and was a close friend of midfielder Neves, having played together for Wolverhampton Wanderers and Portugal.

Supporters appeared to target Al-Hilal midfielder Neves before his side's 6-0 win against Al-Taawoun in the Saudi Pro League on Saturday by repeatedly shouting "Jota" at him.

"The league must take action and punish this kind of fan behaviour," forward Ronaldo, who also plays in the Saudi league for Al-Nassr, wrote on social media.

"This is no longer football, and there have to be limits. People who behave like this should never be allowed to enter a stadium again."

Neves also now wears the number 21 shirt for Portugal in Jota's memory, and has a tattoo on his calf of him and Jota embracing.

Ronaldo played with both players for the national team.

In the footage, Neves can be seen sarcastically applauding a section of fans off-camera, before pointing to the sky and then looking towards them.

After the match, Neves told reporters: "I just hope they don't go to pray later after what they did."

Liverpool forward Jota died alongside his brother Andre Silva in the crash in the Spanish province of Zamora.

He scored 65 goals in 182 appearances for Liverpool after signing from Wolves in 2020, and made his international debut in 2019, scoring 14 goals in 49 games for Portugal.

BBC Sport has contacted both clubs for comment.

articles.title: Rangers 3-0 Celtic: Derek McInnes wins first Old Firm of season as hosts reach Scottish League Cup semi-finals
articles.summary: Report as Rangers comfortably win first Old Firm game of the season 3-0 at Ibrox; Derek McInnes earns his first derby win as manager as his side advance to the semi-finals of the League Cup; Dan Neil and Kevin Kelsy provided the goals on Old Firm debuts with the captain netting twice
articles.body:
Captain Dan Neil notched a double and £9.2m Deadline Day signing Kevin Kelsy was also on the scoresheet on his Old Firm debut at a rapturous Ibrox Stadium - without the presence of away supporters.

Visitors Celtic struggled to cope with Rangers' aggressive man-for-man press - failing to create any distinct opportunities as they lost a first cup tie in seven against their Glasgow rivals.

Kelsy and Minsu Kim both passed up big early opportunities before Neil eventually fired McInnes's side in front after 23 minutes.

The stand-in skipper calmly slotted the ball into the bottom corner with precision from the edge of the area following some great movement and link-up play involving the Rangers' front two of Ryan Naderi and Kelsy.

The Venezuela international then got his first goal for his new club in the second period as he volleyed in Naderi's flick-on at the back post.

Neil completed the scoring with 15 minutes to play as he dispatched the ball into the top corner from the edge of the box to score his second of the afternoon.

Rangers will now face Aberdeen in the semi-finals on the weekend of October 31/November 1, with Hearts drawn against Hibernian.

4: RANGERS SHOULD BE IN FRONT! Johnstone tries to clear the ball but sends it straight to Kelsy. With the keeper off his line, he takes aim but it's wide of the post.

16: OFF THE LINE! Another mistake from Johnstone. The goalkeeper slaps the ball to clear, it goes as far as Minsu. He gets a shot away but Scales is there to clear it off the line.

23: RANGERS GOAL! The hosts take the lead and it's what they deserve. Carter-Vickers fails to clear the danger and Kelsy sends the ball to Neil on the edge of the box to fire into the net.

49: SAVE! A big stop from Johnstone! Rangers with the first chance of the second half, Minsu's effort is pushed clear by the Hoops keeper.

50: SAVE! Rangers go close again. Naderi's close-range header is stopped by Johnstone.

59: RANGERS GOAL! Rangers double their lead as Ibrox bursts back into life. Kelsy makes up for his first-half miss and he smashes Penrice's cross into the net for his first Rangers goal.

64: OFFSIDE GOAL! Raskin got the last touch as Fernandez looked to head in from Penrice. Celtic are all over the place.

72: OVER! Celtic get forward only for Hassan to send his effort over the bar.

76: RANGERS GOAL! Wow! The captain Neil with his second of the afternoon. A curling effort into the top corner and Rangers are all but through to that semi-final draw.

Derek McInnes got his game plan spot on.

He used left-back James Penrice as an auxiliary midfielder to flood the middle of the pitch - allowing Rangers to press Celtic man-for-man.

Djeidi Gassama and Minsu Kim provided width and energy as wing-backs with Dujon Sterling, Emmanuel Fernandez and Olwethu Makhanya defending three-vs-three against Celtic's front line.

It was a bold decision that paid dividends as Celtic folded under the pressure.

Dan Neil snatched the starring role of midfield general from his Celtic counterpart Callum McGregor, who was left isolated without a defensive-minded midfield partner.

McInnes's side now must face the daunting task of a trip to the home of their rivals with no travelling support next Sunday - live on Sky Sports in the Scottish Premiership.

Win that, and the gap is just two points.

"Delighted with the performance of so many today, I don't think we had a failure and that's what it takes to win; that's a good reference for us going forward.

"Obviously we've got to take the good for the game and the feel-good factor and obviously look forward to the semi-final when it comes round, but equally we've got to get ready for the next one.

"The game demanded our full attention today; it demanded a big performance and I'm delighted that we've managed to deliver that.

"You see the strength of the club today, both off the pitch and on the pitch, and I think it does my players no harm at all.

"For the ones who have been here, they'll understand what it means to so many people, but for the ones who are just in the building, it's a good reference for them and good to see what this result means to so many people."

"We were well beaten in the end. The first half we didn't capitalise with a couple of really decent chances when we'd broken their press.

"On the day, just second best. It could be. I think there has to be a realisation of how big this game is.

"It's so important to the fans. It's so important to everybody. Still one of the great fixtures in European football, if not the world and we've got to know that. That's the point.

"We'll have to try and learn from it. We play next Sunday. We've got a midweek game.

"Hopefully it's a wake-up call to look at myself for a start. Then I look at the team. We were second best.

"Did Rangers surprise me? No. I think they're strong. I think they're physically strong. So it'll be a big test for us next Sunday again in every aspect."

articles.title: El Eldense de Messi asalta El Molinón
articles.standfirst: Javi Martínez marcó el gol de la victoria nada más entrar en el campo • Segunda derrota seguida en casa del Sporting • Ferrando se estrena a lo grande en el banquillo azulgrana
articles.summary: Javi Martínez marcó el gol de la victoria nada más entrar en el campo • Segunda derrota seguida en casa del Sporting • Ferrando se estrena a lo grande en el banquillo azulgrana
articles.body: El Eldense, inmerso en el cambio de propiedad y pendiente del desembarco de Leo Messi, asaltó El Molinón para poner punto y final a una semana peculiar. De la salida de Claudio Barragán a ganar en la casa del Sporting. Los rojiblancos volvieron a ser inferiores a un recién ascendido y sumaron su segunda derrota consecutiva. Un solitario gol de Javi Martínez hizo justicia a lo visto en El Molinón y refuerza el proyecto del conjunto del Pepico Amat antes de la llegada del astro argentino. Salió mejor el Eldense de Josep Ferrando. Las internadas de Olabarrieta y Roberto López se le hacían bola a un Sporting que a punto estuvo de abrir el marcador en una picardía de Otero. Fue de lo poco rascable en la primera para los locales. Con una imagen similar al debut ante el Sabadell, era Yáñez el que salvaba al Sporting con una parada estratosférica para responder al disparo desde la frontal de Olabarrieta. El Eldense, valiente y seguro, ganaba en sensaciones. Josep Ferrando siguió alentando a los suyos a ser atrevidos mientras que el Sporting no daba con la tecla. Larcamón cambiaba jugadores, pero no tocaba el sistema. La ocasión más clara de los rojiblancos estuvo en las botas de Iosifov. El ruso, tras una gran acción individual, se estampó con los guantes de Ramón Vila. El Eldense amenazaba con más y una acción brillante de Javi Martínez rompió el cántaro. Un tanto que hizo justicia a la propuesta del Eldense e hizo pagar la racanería del Sporting. De los cuatro partidos que suma en casa en este inicio de curso, Larcamón sólo ha conseguido ganar uno.

articles.title: Sheffield United 0-1 Wolves: Raul Jimenez hits 90th-minute winner to seal narrow win for Cesar Peixoto's side at Bramall Lane
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Sheffield United and Wolverhampton Wanderers at Bramall Lane on Sunday; Raul Jimenez's 90th-minute winner seals a narrow win for Cesar Peixoto's side
articles.body:
Cesar Peixoto's side had controversially been denied a penalty shortly after the restart, when Mark McGuinness handled in the box.

But a game of few clear-cut chances was settled when Jimenez swept in his third goal of the season from close range.

The Blades had both scored and conceded in 14 of their last 15 Championship games at Bramall Lane - so perhaps there was always an inevitability that pattern would not continue.

Chris Wilder's side had just two touches in the opposition box in the first half and generated just 0.06 xG, while at the other end, Marshall Munetsi was Wolves' biggest threat, though Michael Cooper was rarely tested.

With 50 minutes on the clock, Mateus Mane flicked the ball towards goal, with McGuinness' outstretched hand diverting it behind. Referee Rob Jones awarded a corner, nothing more.

Speaking on Sky Sports Football , co-commentator Gary Rowett said: "His arm comes out, it hits him on the end of the arm. I think Sheffield United have probably got away with one there."

Sheffield United debutant Jordan Ayew almost had the perfect introduction when he drove in from the right and flashed a cross-come-shot inches past the far post. But Jimenez had the final say.

Andre located Kieran Trippier, and he moved the ball on for Tommy Doyle to find the Mexican striker, who swept home the decisive goal.

19: CHANCE ! Rodrigo Gomes flashes in a cross to Marshall Munetsi, whose powerful first-time shot is straight at Michael Cooper.

50: NO PENALTY ! Mateus Mane flicks the ball towards goal - and it hits the outstretched hand of Mark McGuinness, but referee Rob Jones signals for a corner.

55: WIDE ! Hugo Bueno seizes on a loose ball and shoots from the edge of the box, with the curl taking his effort narrowly past the right-hand post.

60: Ladislav Krejci pulls Sydie Peck to ground, but avoids a second booking.

67: CLOSE ! Blades debutant Jordan Ayew flashes a shot across the face of goal and just past the post.

90: GOAL ! Raul Jimenez sweeps in the winner from close range to send the away fans wild.

Wilder: Top-end Championship teams can punish you if you switch off

Sheffield United manager Chris Wilder speaking to Sky Sports:

"It's top-end Championship football when you're playing teams like we have done today. They punish you if you just switch off for a moment.

"The players maybe didn't get what they deserved from the game, but that's how the Championship is at times, so we have to roll with that and handle it.

"Especially in the second half, we limited a very attacking team to virtually nothing. I don't think Michael [Cooper] had a save to make.

"It's just disappointing, with the positions we've got into, that we've not found that little bit of quality to get our noses in front."

Peixoto: Subs were important for Wolves - Jimenez is key for us

Wolves head coach Cesar Peixoto speaking to Sky Sports:

"It's an important win for us. We knew it was going to be difficult to play in this stadium against this team. Today, the team was a team for 90 minutes. It was important the guys who came from the bench pushed in the last minutes to try to score. We scored and we won.

"I think we deserved it because we were the better team, but it was a difficult game for us."

On Jimenez : "He's 35 years old, so we have to manage him the best way. He's a key player for us. This week, we have three games, so we had to manage the options. Raul, as a captain, helped the team from the bench, not only with the goal he scored, but he helped to defend the set-pieces."

articles.title: Women's Super League round-up: Chelsea thrash Man Utd to leave Eva Olid still looking for first win
articles.summary: Chelsea win 5-0 at Man Utd as the Blues record their first win of the WSL season; Brighton earn a late point against newly promoted Birmingham, while Everton beat nine-player Charlton; Spurs hold Liverpool and Crystal Palace frustrate Arsenal
articles.body:
Both teams failed to win on the opening weekend of the new campaign, but it was the visitors who dominated proceedings from start to finish in what was a chastening first home game in charge for new United boss Eva Olid.

Chelsea were already in cruise control at half-time after well-taken goals from Sjoeke Nusken and the impressive Keira Walsh, who found the net with a sweetly-struck drive from the edge of the area.

And the visitors continued to dominate in the second period as further goals followed from player-of-the-match Lauren James [61], Ellie Carpenter [65] and - with the last kick of the game - Lucy Bronze.

United's wait for their first league victory of the season goes on ahead of a testing trip to Arsenal on Saturday.

Brighton strike in last second to steal point from Birmingham

Kiko Seike's goal at the very death completed a dramatic comeback for Brighton, who came from two goals down to draw 2-2 with newly promoted Birmingham.

The Blues had proved a stubborn test for champions Manchester City last week and looked set to claim their first three points of the season when Oceane Hurtre and Lily Crosthwaite put them two goals ahead by the 60th minute with a pair of well-taken finishes.

Though the Seagulls piled on the pressure, former goalkeeper Sophie Baggaley was in inspired form, producing a string of saves to preserve her clean sheet.

However, she was let down by her defenders with less than 15 minutes remaining, as Olivia Garcia reacted quickest to her initial save to pull one back. Baggaley was then at fault as the visitors surrendered all three points in cruel fashion, with Seike's effort from a tight angle somehow sneaking underneath the goalkeeper.

More Merseyside woe as Charlton see red against Everton

Charlton saw themselves reduced to nine players at Goodison Park as their resistance was broken late on in a 1-0 defeat to Everton.

After losing 4-0 to Liverpool on the opening weekend, the Addicks produced a much-improved display against the other Merseyside side, but ultimately succumbed to late pressure when Holly McNamara's cross was turned into her own net by Leighanne Robe.

The goal, which came less than 15 minutes from time, arrived after Charlton had already been reduced to 10 players, with Ashleigh Neville shown a straight red card for a high challenge on Ruby Mace. Hawa Cissoko then compounded their misery, picking up two yellow cards in the space of two stoppage-time minutes to leave the Addicks with just nine players at the final whistle.

The defeat leaves newly promoted Charlton second from bottom, only ahead of Man Utd on goal difference.

Liverpool held to frustrating draw by Spurs

Liverpool were held to a frustrating 1-1 draw by Tottenham Hotspur despite dominating the contest at the Totally Wicked Stadium.

However, it was the visitors who went ahead against the run of play and in fortunate circumstances as Signe Gaupset got to the left-hand byline and centered, only for her cross to take a wicked deflection off Sam Kerr before looping into the net over goalkeeper Khiara Keating four minutes before half-time.

Gareth Taylor's side continued to dominate in the second period and deservedly drew level through Aurelie Csillag's near-post header just before the hour mark, however, despite pushing for the winner, they had to settle for a point.

France goalkeeper Pauline Peyraud-Magnin produced an inspired performance between the posts as newly-promoted Crystal Palace drew 0-0 with Arsenal at the Emirates.

The home side had a whopping 30 efforts on goal in the game, nine of which were on target, but could not find a way past the shot stopper, 30, who joined the Eagles on loan last summer.

However, the best chance of the afternoon came Alessia Russo's way nine minutes before the interval, but for once the England international's shooting radar was off as the striker fired past a gaping goal having been picked out with a brilliant left-wing cross.

articles.title: La catana de Kiat: nunca debieron empezar la temporada
articles.standfirst: El hijo de Lim hace caso a Javier Solis y fulmina a toda la 'estructura' deportiva tras sentir la vergüenza del palco en sus propias carnes
articles.summary: El hijo de Lim hace caso a Javier Solis y fulmina a toda la 'estructura' deportiva tras sentir la vergüenza del palco en sus propias carnes
articles.body: La familia Lim llevaba siete años sin pisar Mestalla. No es casualidad que el presidente del club, el hijo Kiat, tuviera que salir corriendo del palco tras la humillación sufrida por el equipo y por su apellido en el partido ante el Barcelona y poco después haya decidido pasar la catana por toda la estructura deportiva que le vendió su amigo y farsante Ron Gourlay. Un amigo valencianista de mucho tiempo me advirtió hace unos meses. "El escocés que han traído es un actor". Hoy mismo sigo con la duda. A Kiat le tocó el orgullo tener que salir de Mestalla a la carrera y con la cabeza gacha delante de un amigo de la familia como Joan Laporta y ese día decidió que Corberán y Gourlay estaban amortizados. Regresó a Singapur a pedir permiso a papá y gastarse los cerca de seis millones de euros que cuesta despedirlos a todos y una vez Peter dio el ok bajó la catana sin ningún tipo de remordimiento. A la calle y otro 'proyecto' nuevo. Era evidente que con la dupla Corberán-Gourlay era imposible salvar la categoría. Entre ambos han confeccionado el equipo más mediocre de la historia del club y claro incluso el hijo de Lim, que muy avispado no parece en cuanto al mundo del fútbol se refiere, se ha dado cuenta de que le estaban timando. Gourlay dijo hace una semana que todo era un paraíso, que el equipo estaba creciendo y mientras el club se desangraba a ojos de todos. La visita de Kiat al partido del Barça fue un golpe para aguantar la gran mentira ante los ojos del hijo del dueño y claro, no ha habido más oportunidades. El único que ha salvado la cabeza es Javier Solís, el director general al que alejaron del fútbol salvándole la cabeza. Todo apunta a que fue él el que susurró al oído de Kiat que o echaba a todos o fuera preparando una legión de trolas para que su padre no le riñera al volver a su país. Corberán y Gourlay nunca debieron empezar la temporada. En un club normal nunca lo hubieran hecho. Pero se aferraron a la mentira de que todo iba sobre ruedas y no hemos superado mitad de septiembre y ya están en la calle. Se lo han ganado a pulso. Ahora el problema es empezar de cero con una plantilla magullada y sin nivel. Los que vengan tienen un reto mayúsculo por delante, pero a poco que trabajen un mínimo el Valencia debe enderezarse. Si eres entrenador y no ganas te echan, si eres CEO de fútbol y no trabajas te echan... aunque la familia Lim esté al mando.

articles.title: Preston North End: Paul Heckingbottom sacked after poor start
articles.summary: Preston North End sack Paul Heckingbottom after six defeats in seven league games left the Lilywhites second bottom of the Championship.
articles.body:
Preston North End have sacked Paul Heckingbottom with the Lilywhites second bottom of the Championship after six defeats in seven games.

Heckingbottom was appointed in August 2024 and took charge of 109 games but has overseen just five wins in 27 league games since the start of January.

Their latest loss came at Deepdale on Saturday as they were beaten 1-0 by Lincoln City as the final whistle was greeted with boos and jeers.

A club statement said: "Football is a results business and despite significant investment in the playing squad since Paul joined, the results during 2026 and the start of this current campaign have not been acceptable.

"Paul leaves us with our thanks and best wishes. His professionalism and work ethic during his time with us have been second to none."

Assistant Stuart McCall has also left the club while coach Jason Euell has been placed in interim charge with a trip to QPR looming on Saturday before the three-week international break follows.

Heckingbottom exit inevitable after months of decline

Draper snatches win for Lincoln at lowly Preston

Preston finished 20th in Heckingbottom's first season at the helm, their lowest finish since returning to the Championship in 2015.

They avoided relegation with a final-day draw at Bristol City but failed to win in their final seven league games, following an FA Cup quarter-final appearance against Aston Villa, secured by thumping Burnley 3-0 in the fifth round.

North End lost only one of their first nine Championship matches in 2025-26, and were among the early pace-setters, but 12 defeats in their final 22 games led to them finishing 14th.

Heckingbottom was backed in the transfer window, with defender Harry Clarke arriving from Ipswich, midfielder Alfie Devine making a permanent move from Tottenham, winger Stan Mills signing from Oxford United, midfielder Leo Leroy joining from Basel and forward Johnny Kenny arriving from Celtic on deadline day.

articles.body: Xavi Espart estrenó este domingo en el Ciutat de València su casillero goleador. El defensa catalán, que ya había firmado dos asistencias en este arranque de competición, fue el encargado de abrir el marcador y marcar el primer tanto del encuentro. Con este gol, el defensa catalán se convirtió en el sexto goleador del Barcelona en este inicio de temporada. Espart, además, continúa demostrando que su aportación al equipo va mucho más allá de las labores defensivas, ya que anteriormente había participado directamente en dos goles gracias a sus asistencias. El zaguero está protagonizando un inicio de curso de ensueño. Xavi Espart se ganó la confianza de Hansi Flick durante la pretemporada y, desde entonces, se ha consolidado como uno de los hombres importantes del equipo. articles.title: Oklahoma State Faces Possible $50K Fine from Big 12 for Fans Storming Field After Upset vs. Oregon
articles.summary: Saturday's stunning 39-31 victory over Oregon was a memorable one for the Oklahoma State football program.
articles.body:
Saturday's stunning 39-31 victory over Oregon was a memorable one for the Oklahoma State football program.

As Front Office Sports noted, Oklahoma State could be facing a $50,000 fine from the Big 12 because its fans stormed the field after the win over the Ducks. They didn't just storm the field, as they tore down the goalpost and carried it all the way to Theta Pond:

According to Kevin Skiver of USA Today , the Big 12's standard fine for field storming is $50,000.

However, he pointed out the conference "has been fairly inconsistent" in its enforcement of such a rule, fining Arizona State last year but then rescinding its fine of Colorado.

"There seems to be a case-by-case nature to the conference's application of the rule, specifically around whether teams follow safety procedures before storming the field," Skiver explained.

Whether the school ends up getting fined or not, Oklahoma State fans celebrating in such a fashion was anything but surprising.

After all, the Ducks arrived as presumed national title contenders with an NFL prospect quarterback in Dante Moore leading the way. Oregon also won last year's matchup 69-3, which was the first of 11 straight losses for the Cowboys.

Mike Gundy's tenure ended during that losing streak, but any high hopes under Eric Morris for the 2026 season ran into an immediate road block when the Cowboys lost by 14 points to Tulsa in the season opener.

Yet somehow they were able to turn things around against one of the most talented rosters in the country, and the eight-point margin of victory doesn't fully capture just how dominant they were in the win.

Oklahoma State outgained Oregon 554-281 in total yardage and had 25 first downs to the visitors' 12. A 96-yard pick six for the Ducks was one of the major mistakes from the home team that kept it closer than those stats indicate, but the Cowboys took the lead for good in the fourth quarter when quarterback Drew Mestemaker soared over multiple defenders for a touchdown.

It was a play that will be remembered for years to come at Oklahoma State and one that set off quite the celebration.

articles.title: Funes: “No podemos esperar a que el tiempo solucione las cosas"
articles.standfirst: El técnico valoró el punto del Málaga en Balaídos
articles.summary: El técnico valoró el punto del Málaga en Balaídos
articles.body: El Málaga CF se marchó de Balaídos con un punto que sabe mejor por el desenlace que por los méritos acumulados durante los 90 minutos. El conjunto blanquiazul volvió a mostrar carencias en ataque y apenas fue capaz de generar peligro ante un Celta que se adelantó por medio de Jutglá y terminó cediendo el empate en la recta final, con el tanto de Adrián Niño Juanfran Funes reconoció las dificultades de su equipo tras el encuentro. El técnico malaguista puso el foco en la falta de determinación en los metros finales y en los problemas que tuvo el Málaga para sacar el balón desde atrás. “Ha sido un partido durísimo, sobre todo por el calor. Hemos dominado, pero no hemos transformado a puerta, nos ha faltado determinación. No vale solo con tener el balón”, explicó Funes, que valoró la capacidad de su equipo para mantenerse en el partido pese a las dificultades. El entrenador del Málaga también admitió que el Celta encontró situaciones peligrosas a la contra, especialmente cuando los malaguistas cometieron errores en la salida. “Nos estaba sorprendiendo el Celta a la contra, estaban esperando el error nuestro. No podemos regalarle, tenemos que cuidarnos más ahí”, señaló. El cambio de estructura en la segunda parte, con la presencia de dos puntas, permitió al Málaga encontrar algo más de profundidad. “Cuando hemos juntado a los dos puntas, hemos encontrado más profundidad”, reconoció Funes. Pese al mal inicio de temporada y a las dificultades que está encontrando el Málaga en su regreso a Primera, Funes aseguró que la confianza dentro del vestuario sigue intacta. “Nuestra confianza es plena, no tenemos duda de a dónde nos pueden llevar”, afirmó. El técnico recordó además que buena parte de su plantilla está debutando en la máxima categoría: “Somos muchos debutantes, todo tiene un proceso. Tenemos el convencimiento de que vamos a ir a mejor”. Funes, no obstante, dejó claro que el equipo no puede esperar de brazos cruzados a que los resultados lleguen con el paso de las jornadas. “No podemos esperar a que el tiempo solucione las cosas. El inconveniente es que pasan las semanas”, advirtió. El preparador lojeño también quiso poner en valor el rendimiento global frente a un rival que compite en Europa. “El Celta ha disparado una vez más que nosotros y no nos ha dominado, hemos tenido más posesión que ellos. No hay una diferencia tan grande con un equipo que juega Europa”, apuntó. El estilo de juego del Málaga volvió a dejar momentos de riesgo en Vigo, pero Funes mantiene su apuesta por la circulación. “Por la forma que jugamos, esa circulación de balón tiene que darnos para que los que entren nos den ese plus de profundidad”, explicó. Funes reconoció, eso sí, que el Málaga tuvo que asumir demasiados riesgos para buscar el empate. “Hasta llegar el gol nuestro, pensaba que estábamos trabajando bien. Sin embargo, íbamos por debajo en el marcador porque les regalamos la oportunidad de la contra”, explicó.

articles.title: Valencia sack head coach Carlos Corberan and chief executive
articles.summary: Valencia sack head coach Carlos Corberan and their football chief executive Ron Gourlay after a winless start to the season.
articles.body:
Valencia have sacked head coach Carlos Corberan and their football chief executive Ron Gourlay after a winless start to the season.

The Spanish side sit bottom of La Liga and have picked up one point from five matches.

In December 2024, Valencia appointed the 43-year-old, who was in charge of Championship side West Bromwich Albion.

Valencia B coach Oscar Sanchez will take over as interim boss.

Valencia, who lost 5-0 to Barcelona last week, finished ninth in La Liga last season, while Corberan guided them to 12th in his first season after joining the club when they were second-bottom of the league.

His first-team coaching staff will also depart the club.

"This decision reflects the club's intention to begin a new phase for the running of the sporting structure and football operations," a club statement said.

"The club will announce the new structure for its football operations and the makeup of the upcoming sporting project shortly."

Former Chelsea chief executive Gourlay, who also worked for West Bromwich Albion, joined Valencia in December 2024.

His team - Lisandro Isei, Hans Gillhaus, Andres Zamora and Malek Shafei - will also leave.

Corberan's successor will be Valencia's 18th permanent head coach since 2012.

Valencia's next fixture is on Tuesday against Deportivo Alaves.

articles.title: Wrexham: Under-pressure Phil Parkinson must bounce back again at Red Dragons
articles.summary: Wrexham boss Phil Parkinson feeling the heat after sluggish start to Championship continued with thrashing at West Ham.
articles.body:
By his own admission, a 6-0 thrashing at West Ham was a low point for Wrexham boss Phil Parkinson during a managerial reign marked by so much success.

The Red Dragons suffered their biggest defeat of Parkinson's tenure at the hands of the Hammers, leaving them 19th in the Championship after seven games.

With a 3-0 victory at Millwall their only win of the campaign, some have questioned whether Parkinson has taken Wrexham as far as he can.

It remains too early to draw a conclusion on that question, but in the eyes of Iwan Roberts, there was no doubt about the performance at West Ham.

He told BBC Radio Wales Sport: "It was an absolutely awful night for Wrexham, although for the first 20 to 25 minutes, they looked hard to break down.

"But once that first goal went in, there was only ever going to be one outcome. It was then a question of how many more West Ham would score."

West Ham rout among 'lowest points' for Wrexham boss

West Ham thrash Wrexham to top Championship

Latest Wrexham news, analysis and fan views

West Ham scored four times in the second half, including one less than two minutes after the restart, as Wrexham were torn apart.

"If it was a boxing match, the coach would have thrown the towel in," Roberts added.

"There was a lack of work, communication, organisation, a lack of players wanting to be brave in a difficult situation, and you can't accept that as football fans.

"If there was a measuring tape of where Wrexham are against a team who have been in the Premier League for many, many years, this was it.

Parkinson has been under pressure before during his Wrexham tenure, and even felt the heat when the Red Dragons made a slow start to life in the second tier last season.

Wrexham won just five of their first 15 league games in 2025-26 - and drew six times - before eventually falling just short of the play-off places.

Many pointed to that inconsistent start as the reason why Wales' oldest club ultimately finished two points away from a shot at promotion.

After another summer with £30m spent in the transfer market, and two extra play-off spots up for grabs, the expectation is to go one better.

Former Wrexham midfielder Waynne Phillips does not doubt there is pressure on Parkinson, but believes the 58-year-old manager can turn things around again.

"I'm not surprised to see the reaction that comes after the game - this is how it has been for years around Wrexham," he told BBC Radio Cymru.

"I remember in the National League, if Wrexham went a game or two without winning, everyone would want Phil Parkinson out.

"But he's someone who can bounce back really well. He's been about long enough to know there will be difficult periods and difficult nights.

"I don't think Parkinson will be worrying about the noise around him, but he will worry about what he saw on Friday night."

Former Wales defender Danny Gabbidon echoed those sentiments, and believes Parkinson - the architect of so many promotions - should be afforded time.

"Pressure will start to build if those terrible results continue, but it's still very early in the season," he said on BBC Radio Wales.

"If you are slightly off it and not on your game, West Ham are capable of doing that to you. Phil Parkinson will hope it's a bad day at the office.

"Sometimes when you get those results, it wakes everybody up. Wrexham have been so good for so long now. They've charged through the divisions.

"There is no need to panic yet. We should allow the manager some time after he has been so good over the previous seasons, but you could sense his frustration after the game."

The summer signings have been a hot topic among Wrexham commentators.

While money was invested in the squad, only two players - Issa Kabore and Jacques Ekomie - have top-flight experience.

Phillips, who made over 200 appearances for Wrexham, is not convinced that some of the recruits have upgraded the side.

"It took a while last season for the new signings to settle, but up to now, I've not seen enough from the new players to believe they improve on what Wrexham had," he said.

"But one win brings another very quickly, and suddenly confidence grows. I don't for a second think that these are not good footballers.

"To come into a new club, it takes time sometimes. You're lucky if it happens from the first game.

"The goalkeeper, Anthony Patterson, has done alright, even though he conceded six goals at West Ham, so there will be questions about him.

"I haven't seen enough from Ben Whiteman in midfield to say that he's better than what they had last season.

"Callum O'Hare hardly had a kick at West Ham. There is room for them to improve, but the same is true for those who were there last season."

Wrexham will hope they can end the first block of Championship games on a high note by beating Southampton before the international break.

The Red Dragons are yet to win at home this season, and were thumped 5-1 by Saints at the Racecourse last season.

That heavy April defeat had been the only time Parkinson's Wrexham leaked five goals in a single league game since 2023, and they can ill afford a repeat.

articles.title: Giráldez se queja por jugar a más de 30 grados: "Me encantaría haber ganado para poder hablar más de este tema..."
articles.standfirst: El técnico lamenta que se les escaparon dos puntos
articles.summary: El técnico advierte sobre los riesgos de jugar a altísimas temperaturas
articles.body: Claudio Giráldez cree que merecieron más contra el Málaga y que nuevamente se les escapó la victoria, ve mejora en su equipo y advierte sobre los riesgos de jugar a altísimas temperaturas como este domingo en Vigo. Partido: "Sensación de perder 2 puntos nuevamente. Llevo con esa sensación en 4-5 partidos de los que hemos jugado hasta ahora. Los partidos tienen momentos, hay que matarlos. Creo que el equipo ha hecho muchísimas cosas bien en un día de calor en el que hay que dar la enhorabuena a todos los jugadores por el esfuerzo que han hecho porque se han jugado su físico y su integridad". Complicaciones: "Estamos en ese momento en el que con muy poco se nos están escapando puntos, en el que ayer perdemos a Jones en el entrenamiento, Borja no llega. Hoy a Pablo Durán le da un golpe de calor y no es capaz ni de estar en el banquillo. Iago entra y se lesiona en la primera acción que tiene". Confianza: "A seguir trabajando, a confiar en los jugadores, en esta plantilla que tantas alegrías nos ha dado y a seguir en la línea ascendente en la que creo que estamos". Jugar a altísima temperatura con espectadores atendidos en la grada: "Me encantaría haber ganado para poder hablar más de este tema porque cuando no ganas si hablas de estas cosas parece que es una pataleta de un entrenador, una excusa, una queja. Estoy convencido que Iago no se hubiese lesionado en otras circunstancias, estoy convencido que Pablo Durán hubiese podido jugar el partido. Estoy convencido que la gente hubiese disfrutado más. Hubiese venido más gente, el ambiente hubiese sido distinto. El espectáculo entre dos equipos que quieren jugar al fútbol hubiese sido mejor". Jugándose el físico: "Hay un riesgo de lesión de los protagonistas, que son los jugadores y a veces se olvida eso. Es nuestro sexto partido en tres semanas. Hemos jugado los últimos dos a más de 30º. No creo que sea lo ideal". Optimista: "Hoy es el partido en el que más tiempo hemos estado dominando la situación, probablemente el que menos posesión hemos tenido pero desde un control total y acabará saliendo como nos ha pasado el año pasado, cuando la gente siga unida, cuando sigamos apoyando al compañero, a nuestros jugadores. Es el camino. A mí me ha gustado mucho más el partido".

articles.body: Aitor Mañas ya está de vuelta en Vitoria después de haber permanecido en observación durante la última noche tras el fuerte golpe en la cabeza que sufrió ayer en El Sardinero. El canterano babazorro hizo saltar todas las alarmas tras chocar con José Salinas en una disputa aérea y dar muestras de estar aturdido pese a que estuvo consciente en todo momento. El ariete tuvo que ser evacuado en ambulancia rumbo al hospital tras sufrir una conmoción cerebral como consecuencia de un traumatismo craneoencefálico. Después de haber recibido el alta hospitalaria, Mañas tendrá que cumplir con el protocolo de actuación ante una conmoción cerebral establecido por la Asociación Española de Médicos de Equipos de Fútbol (AEMEF) y causará baja en los dos próximos compromisos ligueros. Quique Sánchez Flores no podrá contar con el ‘20’ este martes en la visita del Valencia a Mendizorroza y tampoco podrá hacerlo el próximo sábado en el segundo derbi de la temporada ante el Athletic. Por suerte para el técnico madrileño, Toni Martínez reapareció ayer en la segunda mitad ante el Racing y aspira a ser una de las novedades dentro de 48 horas frente al conjunto ché.

articles.title: Coventry 0-5 Brighton: Lewis Dunk scores stunner in big win for Seagulls as Frank Lampard’s side stay bottom
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Brighton won 5-0 at Coventry to move into the top four of the Premier League table and leave Frank Lampard’s side bottom – still waiting for their first point and their first goal. Taiwo Awoniyi was sent off for the home side
articles.body:
Charalampos Kostoulas put the Seagulls in charge before the interval, Malick Yalcouye doubled the lead after the break, and when Taiwo Awonoyi was sent off there was no way back. Pascal Gross' penalty, Lewis Dunk's rocket and Yasin Ayari's strike sealed it.

Brighton had the first seven shots of the match, all inside the first 20 minutes, but Coventry had the next eight and were in the ascendancy - which is what will make Kostoulas' opener more frustrating for Lampard. The Greek striker punished them.

The first half featured 21 shots, the most in any Premier League game so far this season, but Bart Verbruggen kept Coventry out despite the home side having 10 of them. He tipped Jack Rudoni's volley wide and Frank Onyeka's vicious strike over the crossbar.

There was to be no comeback for Lampard's side. The start of the second half put paid to that when Yalcouye nipped in ahead of a sluggish Aurele Florian Amenda to race through and slot home before Taiwo Awoniyi was sent off for elbowing Maxin De Cuyper.

When Bobby Thomas tripped Kostoulas, things got worse for the Sky Blues. Gross converted the penalty to make it three and then Dunk took a pot-shot from distance that arrowed into the top corner of Carl Rushworth's net. Yasin Ayari then made it five in stoppage time.

Brighton, the Premier League top scorers, go fourth. As for Coventry, their fans were impressively defiant in their support but they remain bottom without a goal let alone a point upon their Premier League return. Hull and Ipswich have started well. They have not.

articles.title: Rangers 3-0 Celtic: What we learned from Old Firm League Cup clash ahead of first Premiership meeting of season
articles.summary: It was victory for Rangers manager Derek McInnes in his first Old Firm clash with Celtic; they will now face Aberdeen in the League Cup semi-finals; Celtic host Rangers in the first Premiership meeting of season on September 20, live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Dan Neil's two perfectly precise strikes from the edge of the area and Kevin Kelsy's back-post volley were symptomatic of the level of control that Derek McInnes' side enjoyed in the game.

Aggressive, front-footed, confident - they were everything that Martin O'Neill's side were not.

Ahead of the second meeting between the two sides in the space of a week - live on Sky Sports - here is what we learned from the first clash of the new season.

The Rangers boss humbly shrugged off any suggestion of a tactical masterplan in his post-match news conference - but he was just being modest.

McInnes got his game plan spot on, and Celtic couldn't live with his team.

He used left-back James Penrice as an auxiliary midfielder to flood the middle of the pitch - allowing Rangers to press Celtic man-for-man.

Djeidi Gassama and Minsu Kim provided width and energy as wing-backs with Dujon Sterling, Emmanuel Fernandez and Olwethu Makhanya defending three-vs-three against Celtic's front line.

It was a bold decision that paid dividends as Celtic folded under the pressure.

Dan Neil snatched the starring role of midfield general from his Celtic counterpart Callum McGregor, who was left isolated without a defensive-minded midfield partner.

The former Sunderland man would probably have still been named Player of the Match even if he had not netted two famous derby goals.

After Rangers scored their third, Celtic's usually imperious captain McGregor ordered his own defence "no more goals".

A sobering submission from a figurehead who has been the heartbeat of so many Old Firm victories - but perhaps a signal of a deeper-rooted problem.

Celtic are leaking goals at an alarming rate in big games.

Their now infamous precipitous collapse against LASK from 4-0 up in their Champions League play-off round qualifier is no longer an anomaly. In the two biggest games of Celtic's season so far, they have shipped nine consecutive goals without reply.

A team that has been lauded for the strength of their mentality and togetherness is now showing early signs of mental fragility when faced with the intangible pressure of a 'big game', and the very tangible threat of aggressive, direct and physical opposition.

While Sunday's defeat is nowhere near as humiliating as that fateful evening in Linz, it must serve as a wake-up call for the Scottish champions if they dared to believe they could canter to another title.

There were no away fans inside Ibrox on Sunday, and there will also be no travelling support at Celtic Park next weekend.

It's impossible to measure what, if any, impact that had on Celtic's lacklustre display or Rangers' rampant performance. However, the result heaps pressure on next week's hosts, who will be met by 60,000 scarred supporters expecting a response.

On paper, the champions go into the game with a 100 percent league record, but psychologically, their impressive start pales in significance to the trauma inflicted upon them following a beating at the hands of their fiercest rivals.

Perhaps the Hoops will embody the spirit of a wounded animal, perhaps Rangers will too crumble without the safety net of their own support, or perhaps any logical or rational thinking applied to attempting to predict the outcome of an Old Firm game will once again be rendered useless.

The only certainty is that next week's Scottish Premiership meeting - live on Sky Sports - is more consequential. Ahead of a three-week-long international break, the gap at the top of the table will stand at either two, five or eight points.

articles.title: Tom English: 'McInnes delivers togetherness & intensity in Old Firm gobsmacker'
articles.summary: BBC Scotland's chief sportswriter Tom English analyses Rangers' convincing Old Firm victory over Celtic at Ibrox.
articles.body:
Fifty five minutes into this Rangers romp at Ibrox, Martin O'Neill and Shaun Maloney stood beside each other in the Celtic technical area, chin-stroking, head-scratching, pointing, waving, drowning.

To them, in this moment, this Premier Sports Cup quarter-final must have felt like a surreal and nightmarish occasion - and it was only 1-0 at the time. Rangers had really only started to wreak their havoc.

Such was Rangers' dominance, their complete owning of their visitors in every conceivable category, the Celtic managerial brains trust seemed just as lost as every one of their players on the field.

Man for man, Rangers won every battle, not for 45 minutes but for the full ninety.

Rangers overwhelm meek Celtic to clinch semi-final spot

No away fans, of course. Not that that had anything to do with it. Being locked out of Ibrox might have seemed like a curse to Celtic folk. In the end, it must have felt like the greatest blessing.

In his early months in the job, Derek McInnes has been looking for a marquee performance. Now he has it. He was looking for a formation that worked and personnel that were big enough and bold enough to execute it and he got that, too. This was 3-0 going on more. Plenty more.

The simplicity of their progression to the semi-final was a touch surreal. Neither of these were in particularly good form coming into this. They were both winning, yes, but they haven't been all that convincing.

This season, in their last eight domestic features combined - all won, in fairness - there was only a goal in it at the end in seven of them. Both sides had got themselves into a cycle of missed chances and, at times, uncomfortable days.

So the smart money was on a tight contest. Extra-time, maybe. Penalties? You wouldn't have ruled that out either. O'Neill is such a winning machine that many would have expected Celtic to find a way, somehow. So much for that.

Few Old Firm games surprise you anymore, but this one was a gobsmacker.

Rangers had all the intensity and all the togetherness. They had six players making their Old Firm debut from the start but if inexperience can be a challenge in this fixture then it was a challenge they met with gusto.

McInnes and his driven and vastly superior players neutralised Celtic, shut them down, rendered them impotent. Celtic captain Callum McGregor lords it over days like this, but the supreme central midfielder was Dan Neil, not just in his outstanding goals but in the control and the leadership he exerted.

With Nico Raskin beside him it was a no-contest in the middle of the pitch. James Penrice did a power of really good work in there, too.

Camilo Duran, playing wide again instead of through the middle, has been one of the players of the season so far, but he hardly existed, totally bossed by Olwethu Makhanya - calm in the maelstrom, classy in nearly everything he did.

Kasper Hogh needed a goal having scored in just one game in six - a hat-trick, albeit - but the record signing spent much of his day in Emmanuel Fernandez's pocket. He had no service and no sniff.

'McInnes might have hit on something substantial'

Where did this come from? Lord knows, but it makes life very interesting now, not just in the destination of the League Cup - Rangers will be massive favourites against Aberdeen in their semi-final - but in the race for the league title.

McInnes might have hit on something substantial. The big task, of course, is to repeat that energy, that belief, that ruthlessness.

You expected Celtic to stir and make a game of it, but they were never allowed to, in part because of their own awful shortcomings with the ball and in other part because Rangers didn't allow them to settle. They hunted them down, right from the opening minutes.

A mood, of sorts, was set as early as the fourth minute when Sam Johnstone, Celtic's jumpy new goalkeeper, passed a clearance straight to Kevin Kelsy, who slashed it wide.

Johnstone had been harried by Rangers' press, a big theme of the day. For Kelsy, it was a great chance to strike early, but if he failed then he made amends later on.

Kelsy is only in the door, but he looks to have personality and desire. He was playing with Ryan Naderi, an oft-criticised striker, a player you hear constantly is not Rangers class. Naderi was one of the totems of the day, a work rate that never stopped, a constant menace in hunting and gathering. Naderi might have changed a few Rangers minds on Sunday.

The opener was a microcosm; Naderi robbing Cameron Carter-Vickers, Kelsy then picking out Neil for a sumptuous finish. Rangers were physically and creatively on top, but there's always a feeling that one goal needed to become two to halt Celtic's assumed purple patch, a response that never came.

That was the bizarre thing. Total authority for an entire game is a rare enough thing in this contest. Usually there's a spell when the team that's ahead has to weather some kind of storm. Celtic couldn't throw a bucket of water in Rangers' direction not to mind a tempest. When McInnes' side made it two it was only what they deserved.

Penrice put in the cross, Naderi flicked it on and Kelsy banged in the volley. Neil's second and Rangers' third was a peach, a sign of confident uninhibited players enjoying themselves. The smallest of mercies for Celtic was that it stayed at three.

The second part of this drama comes on Sunday, a league game that could not have been better set up had Eddie Hearn been involved in the promotion. Rangers looking to lay down another marker going to Celtic's home, full of 60,000 folk baying for revenge. Given some of the vile songs that were directed at O'Neill at Ibrox then McInnes is in for some treatment. Sadly, he's heard it all over before, as has O'Neill.

McInnes was measured in the aftermath, more low-key than you might have expected and there was sense in that. This was one game and he knew it. They won nothing on the back of it and he knew that, too.

Apart from, that is, precious momentum and self-belief and the knowledge of what their standard can be when they get it right. And on Sunday, they got it spectacularly right.

articles.title: Brighton thrash ten-man Coventry as Sky Blues remain pointless and goalless
articles.summary: Coventry 0-5 Brighton: Charalampos Kostoulas, Malick Yalcouye, Pascal Gross, Lewis Dunk and Yasin Ayari all scored for the Seagulls
articles.body:
Brighton inflicted a severe 5-0 defeat on 10-man Coventry , handing the home side their fourth consecutive loss in the Premier League.

Coventry remain the sole team in the division yet to register a single point this season, having failed to score a goal throughout this four-match losing streak.

An entertaining first half saw both teams trade opportunities, producing 21 shots in total — the highest tally recorded in the opening 45 minutes of any Premier League fixture so far this campaign.

However, it was Charalampos Kostoulas who provided the breakthrough, converting his first league goal since January to ensure the away side went into the break with a lead.

Coventry's afternoon went from bad to worse early in the second half. Malick Yalcouye scored Brighton 's second within nine minutes of the restart, shortly before Taiwo Awoniyi received a red card for an elbow on Maxim De Cuyper.

The visiting side then flexed their muscles to complete the rout. Pascal Gross converted a penalty for the third, Lewis Dunk hammered home an effort from 25 yards, and Yasin Ayari capped off a five-star performance for the Seagulls with a fifth.

From the opening whistle, Brighton displayed an eagerness to shoot on sight. Olivier Boscagli demonstrated their confidence inside the first 15 minutes by attempting a speculative shot from inside his own half, though Carl Rushworth was not required to worry.

Further early opportunities fell to Yalcouye and Kostoulas, but neither managed to work the Coventry goalkeeper.

The hosts tried to show what they had at the top end of the pitch and got their first effort on target when Ephron Mason-Clark scuffed a shot into the hands of Bart Verbruggen , before Jack Rudoni saw a header skim the crossbar.

Coventry grew into the contest, forcing Verbruggen to stop a couple of volleys from both Rudoni and Frank Onyeka .

Just as it looked like Coventry had established a foothold in the game, Brighton broke the deadlock in the 35th minute. Kostoulas latched on to a header from Gross, took a couple of neat touches, and fired a low, hard shot into the bottom left corner.

Brighton doubled their advantage six minutes after the break when Yalcouye beat two defenders before racing through on goal and slotting past Rushworth.

Coventry were forced to play the majority of the second half with a man less after Awoniyi caught De Cuyper with a flailing elbow, which referee Tony Harrington deemed dangerous enough for a direct red card.

The home side's afternoon deteriorated further when Bobby Thomas brought down Kostoulas inside the area, allowing Gross to slot away the resulting penalty.

Brighton's outstanding day continued to improve as Dunk decided to let fly from 25 yards with a strike that flew into the top left corner.

There was still time for the away side to add a fifth, with Ayari trying his luck from range with a lovely curling effort that once again beat Rushworth.

articles.title: Phil Foden sent off in Manchester derby for wild kick on Bruno Fernandes
articles.summary: Foden become the first Manchester City player to be sent off in the derby since 2006
articles.body:
Phil Foden was sent off in the 23rd minute of the Manchester derby after kicking out at Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes .

The Stockport-born Foden became the first Manchester City player to be sent off in the derby since 2006 and left his team down to 10 men at Old Trafford.

The incident came midway through an even first half of the Premier League clash.

Foden was challenged by Fernandes near the touchline and fell to the ground on top of the ball.

Fernandes kicked the bottom of Foden's back as he attempted to get through to the ball.

Foden reacted angrily and, while lying on the ground, kicked up and out at Fernandes with both feet, appearing to catch him in the stomach.

The 26-year-old was shown a straight-red card by referee Michael Oliver and the decision was checked and then backed-up by VAR.

According to the Premier League Match Centre, referee Oliver saw a "kick out into the body of Bruno" from Foden.

The VAR official Matt Donohue then confirmed: "That looks like a clear red card to me. Looks to be a secondary movement."

Fernandes was not punished for the role he played after initially kicking Foden while the Manchester City forward was on the ground.

It was seen as a lucky escape for the Portuguese, according to former Manchester United defender Gary Neville.

"I am surprised that Fernandes has got away without a booking," Neville said during his commentary on Sky Sports .

It was the first red card of Foden's Premier League career, after 228 appearances, and City's first in this fixture since Bernardo Corradi in 2006.

Leeds are a reliable team to bet on. You know exactly what you're going to get. I do like that home win but I also like the prospects of Matias Fernandez-Pardo drawing cards for Newcastle.
